EU ETS revisions: Consideration of amendments
On 4 November 2026, ENVI Members considered jointly the amendments that were tabled to the revision of the EU Emission Trading System (EU ETS) Directive and to the closely linked proposal for a regulation to simplify and streamline monitoring, reporting and verification of the CO2 emissions for the maritime transport (MRV Regulation).
The Commission proposals aim to align the EU ETS with the legally binding climate target of 90% reduction in net GHG emissions compared to 1990 levels by 2040. It encompasses the following: adjusting the emissions reduction trajectory from 2031 onwards; considering the use of a limited quantity of high-quality international carbon credits; integrating domestic permanent carbon removals into the EU ETS; a reform of the market stability reserve (MSR); extending the free allocation of EU ETS allowances and indirect carbon cost compensation beyond 2030; and increased financial support for innovation and decarbonization investments. All together, 3435 amendments were tabled: 3266 on the EU ETS Directive and 169 on the MRV Regulation.
The amendments touch upon all elements of the proposals, including the emissions reduction trajectory, the use of ETS revenues, international carbon credits and carbon removals, carbon price stability, and the scope (inclusion of municipal waste incinerations, MSR, funding instruments and extension of coverage in maritime and aviation sectors).
